tldr: We compare two predetermined perfect matching plans with outcomes in \(0\le y_e\le B\) and a hard limit of \(b\) unused matches on every draw. For one cycle at zero budget the minimax risks are exactly \(RU=B^2/4\), \(RA=B^2\), and \(RH=4B^2\). The note proves single-cycle risk brackets and a multi-component water-filling bracket; exact cross-component allocation remains open. Componentwise maximal augmentation also proves a shared-budget plateau: for \(b\ge b_{\mathrm{sat}}=\sum_j\lfloor n_j/3\rfloor\), the unrestricted, unbiased-affine, and fixed-share product risks equal their no-floor counterparts. Sharp positive-budget values, no-floor tensorization, and any gain from correlated allocation remain open.
